capability_conclusions: No Wine of any version is installed. Every Wine-dependent Gate 0 check is BLOCKED.
No compiler (gcc/make) is present, so probes requiring compilation are BLOCKED.
Kernel is 6.6; ntsync requires 6.14 or later, so ntsync behaviour cannot be exercised here even if Wine were installed.
No dpkg foreign architecture is enabled, so 32-bit Windows binaries could not be exercised without enabling i386.
WSLg provides a display, but there is no desktop environment, no portal backend and no StatusNotifierItem host, so no desktop-integration claim can be tested here.
The GPU is reachable only through the WSL2 driver path, which is not representative of a native Linux graphics stack, so no graphics or driver claim can be tested here.
Neither available filesystem supports reflink copies, so the reflink-based snapshot mechanism proposed in ADR-0017 cannot be exercised on this host.

what_would_unblock.graphics_checks: Native Linux with a real Mesa or NVIDIA driver stack.
what_would_unblock.integration_checks: A real desktop session (GNOME or KDE) with xdg-desktop-portal and a StatusNotifierItem host.
what_would_unblock.recovery_checks: A filesystem with reflink support (btrfs or XFS) or an explicit decision to use full copies.
what_would_unblock.wine_dependent_checks: An approved lab with Wine installed at a pinned version, ideally on a native Linux install rather than WSL2.
